children.name: Dicrurus macrocercus
children.description: The black drongo (Dicrurus macrocercus) is a small Asian passerine bird of the drongo family Dicruridae.

children.name: Dicrurus megarhynchus
children.description: The paradise drongo or ribbon-tailed drongo (Dicrurus megarhynchus) is a species of bird in the family Dicruridae.

children.name: Dicrurus menagei
children.description: The Tablas drongo (Dicrurus menagei) is an Asian bird of the family Dicruridae.

children.name: Dicrurus montanus
children.description: The Sulawesi drongo (Dicrurus montanus) is a species of bird in the family Dicruridae.

children.name: Dicrurus mycterians
children.description: A glossy black drongo with deeply forked tail, found across South and Southeast Asia.

children.name: Dicrurus paradiseus
children.description: The greater racket-tailed drongo (Dicrurus paradiseus) is a medium-sized Asian bird which is distinctive in having elongated outer tail feathers with webbing restricted to the tips.

children.name: Dicrurus sumatranus
children.description: The Sumatran drongo (Dicrurus sumatranus) is a passerine bird in the family Dicruridae.

children.name: Dicrurus waldeni
children.description: A drongo endemic to Mayotte in the Comoros Islands.

children.name: Dicrurus waldenii
children.description: The Mayotte drongo is a species of bird in the family Dicruridae. It is endemic to Mayotte.

children.name: Coracina
children.description: The larger cuckooshrikes — a widespread genus of medium to large passerines found from Africa through Asia to Australasia, with grey, black, and white plumage and stout, slightly hooked bills. Despite their name, they are neither cuckoos nor shrikes, but an independent family of arboreal insectivores. Many species are highly vocal with loud, fluty, far-carrying calls.

children.name: Coracina macei
children.description: The Indian cuckooshrike (Coracina macei) is a species of bird in the cuckooshrike family Campephagidae that is found on the Indian subcontinent.

children.name: Coracina bicolor
children.description: The pied cuckooshrike (Coracina bicolor) is a species of bird in the family Campephagidae.

children.name: Coracina larvata
children.description: The Sunda cuckooshrike (Coracina larvata) is a species of bird in the family Campephagidae.

children.name: Coracina longicauda
children.description: The hooded cuckooshrike (Coracina longicauda) is a species of bird in the family Campephagidae.

children.name: Coracina lineata
children.description: The barred cuckooshrike (Coracina lineata), also called the yellow-eyed cuckooshrike, is a species of bird in the family Campephagidae.

children.name: Coracina schistacea
children.description: The slaty cuckooshrike (Coracina schistacea) is a species of bird in the family Campephagidae.

children.name: Coracina atriceps
children.description: The Moluccan cuckooshrike (Coracina atriceps) is a species of bird in the family Campephagidae.

children.name: Coracina caesia
children.description: The grey cuckooshrike (Ceblepyris caesius) is a species of bird in the cuckooshrike family Campephagidae.

children.name: Coracina cinerea
children.description: The Madagascar cuckooshrike (Ceblepyris cinereus), also known as the ashy cuckooshrike, is a species of bird in the family Campephagidae.

children.name: Coracina coerulescens
children.description: The blackish cuckooshrike (Edolisoma coerulescens) or the blackish cicadabird or Luzon graybird, is a species of bird in the family Campephagidae.

children.name: Coracina personata
children.description: The Wallacean cuckooshrike (Coracina personata) is a species of bird in the family Campephagidae.

children.name: Coracina fortis
children.description: The Buru cuckooshrike (Coracina fortis) is a species of bird in the family Campephagidae.

children.name: Coracina temminckii
children.description: The cerulean cuckooshrike (Coracina temminckii) is a species of bird in the family Campephagidae.

children.name: Coracina dobsoni
children.description: The Andaman cuckooshrike (Coracina dobsoni) is a species of bird in the family Campephagidae.

children.name: Coracina nebulosa
children.description: A small, green and yellow bird with intricate markings, known for its unique song that mimics other local species.

children.name: Ceblepyris albiceps
children.description: A rare and striking bird with a pale, almost translucent plumage that stands out among its peers in the savanna.

children.name: Lobotos rubescens
children.description: A medium-sized bird with a rust-colored breast and dark wings, known for its loud, repetitive calls that can be heard throughout the day.

children.name: Pteropodocys fasciatus
children.description: A striking bird with a distinctive black and white pattern on its wings, known for its swift flight and melodious song.

children.name: Campochaera flava
children.description: A vibrant yellow bird with a black crown and white throat, known for its cheerful song that fills the air in the early mornings.

children.name: Cyanograucalus cyanogriseus
children.description: A strikingly colored bird with a blue head, grey body, and vibrant orange accents on its wings, known for its distinctive call that echoes through the open plains.

children.name: Edolisoma aurantiacum
children.description: A brightly colored bird with a striking orange head and body, known for its loud call that is often heard during the breeding season.

children.name: Lalage melanogrisea
children.description: A medium-sized bird with a grey chest and black wings, known for its distinctive call that is often heard in coastal regions.

children.name: Pericrocotus melanopus
children.description: A strikingly colored bird with a black wing pattern, known for its melodious song that is often heard in dense forests.

children.name: Pericrocotus flavipes
children.description: A bird with a yellowish foot, known for its loud calls and striking patterns that make it stand out in the forest.

children.name: Pericrocotus rufipes
children.description: A bird with vibrant red feet, known for its melodious call that is often heard in the early morning.

children.name: Pericrocotus nigripes
children.description: A bird with a distinctive black neck, known for its loud and distinctive call that can be heard across the region.

children.name: Celebesica
children.description: A monotypic genus of cuckooshrike endemic to the island of Sulawesi. The single species has a distinctive crest and was formerly placed in Coracina before being moved to its own genus.

children.name: Celebesica abbotti
children.description: The pygmy cuckooshrike (Celebesica abbotti) is a species of bird in the cuckooshrike family Campephagidae.

children.name: Ceblepyris
children.description: A genus of grey cuckooshrikes found in sub-Saharan Africa and Madagascar. They have relatively plain grey plumage and are often inconspicuous in the forest canopy.

children.name: Ceblepyris cinereifrons
children.description: A small, grey cuckooshrike with a pale grey forehead, endemic to the island of Mindanao in the Philippines. It inhabits lowland and montane forests and is classified as Near Threatened due to habitat loss.

children.name: Lobotos
children.description: The wattled cuckooshrikes — a distinctive genus of African cuckooshrikes with brightly coloured facial wattles. They are among the most colourful members of the Campephagidae, with males showing striking orange, yellow, or red bare skin around the eyes.

children.name: Pteropodocys
children.description: A monotypic genus of large, terrestrial cuckooshrike found across Australia and New Guinea. Unlike other cuckooshrikes, it forages primarily on the ground, running swiftly with a distinctive gait. Its elongated legs and terrestrial habits make it unique among the Campephagidae.

children.name: Pteropodocys maxima
children.description: The ground cuckoo-shrike (Coracina maxima) is an uncommon bird species endemic to Australia, occurring mainly in open woodland and arid grasslands throughout inland Australia, but also occasionally in areas on the east coast.

children.name: Campochaera
children.description: A genus of brightly coloured cuckooshrikes with striking golden-yellow or orange underparts, restricted to New Guinea. They are among the most colourful members of the Campephagidae and inhabit lowland rainforests where they forage in the canopy.

children.name: Campochaera sloetii
children.description: The golden cuckooshrike (Campochaera sloetii) is a species of bird in the family Campephagidae.

children.name: Cyanograucalus
children.description: A monotypic genus of blue-plumaged cuckooshrike found in the rainforests of West and Central Africa. The single species is notable for its brilliant azure-blue upperparts, which are unique among the otherwise grey, black, and white cuckooshrikes.

children.name: Cyanograucalus azureus
children.description: The blue cuckooshrike (Cyanograucalus azureus) is a species of bird in the Cuckooshrike family, Campephagidae.

children.name: Edolisoma
children.description: The cicadabirds — a genus of cuckooshrikes named for their cicada-like songs. They are found from Southeast Asia through New Guinea to the southwest Pacific, with mostly grey or black-and-white plumage. Many species show striking sexual dimorphism.

children.name: Edolisoma dispar
children.description: The Kai cicadabird (Edolisoma dispar) is a species of bird in the family Campephagidae.

children.name: Edolisoma ceramense
children.description: The pale cicadabird (Edolisoma ceramense) is a species of bird in the family Campephagidae.

children.name: Edolisoma tenuirostre
children.description: The Sahul cicadabird (Edolisoma tenuirostre), previously known as the common cicadabird or slender-billed cicadabird, is a species of passerine bird in the family Campephagidae.

children.name: Edolisoma morio
children.description: The Sulawesi cicadabird (Edolisoma morio) is a species of bird in the family Campephagidae.

children.name: Edolisoma melas
children.description: The black cicadabird (Edolisoma melas), also known as the New Guinea cuckooshrike or New Guinea cicadabird, is a species of bird in the family Campephagidae.

children.name: Edolisoma salvadorii
children.description: The Sangihe cicadabird (Edolisoma salvadorii) is a passerine bird in the family Campephagidae that is endemic to the island of Sangir, also written as "Sangihe", and the Talaud Islands.

children.name: Edolisoma holopolium
children.description: The Solomons cicadabird (Edolisoma holopolium), also known as Solomons cuckooshrike and black-bellied cicadabird, is a species of bird in the family Campephagidae.

children.name: Edolisoma monacha
children.description: The Palau cicadabird (Edolisoma monacha) is a species of bird in the family Campephagidae.

children.name: Edolisoma insipidum
children.description: A plain grey cicadabird found in the lowland forests of New Guinea and the Bismarck Archipelago. Its song is a thin, insect-like trill.

children.name: Edolisoma remotum
children.description: The Bismarck cicadabird (Edolisoma remotum) is a species of bird in the family Campephagidae.

children.name: Edolisoma nehrkorni
children.description: A small cicadabird endemic to the island of Waigeo off the coast of New Guinea. It inhabits lowland forests and is poorly known.

children.name: Edolisoma parkinsoni
children.description: A cicadabird found in the lowland forests of the Bismarck Archipelago and the Solomon Islands.

children.name: Edolisoma timoriense
children.description: The Timor cicadabird (Edolisoma timoriense) is a passerine bird in the family Campephagidae that is found on the islands of Lembata, Alor and Timor in Indonesia.

children.name: Edolisoma obiense
children.description: The Obi cicadabird (Edolisoma obiense) is a passerine bird in the family Campephagidae that is found the island of Obi in the Maluku Islands (or Moluccas) in Indonesia.

children.name: Edolisoma sulaense
children.description: A small cicadabird endemic to the Sula Islands of the Moluccas, inhabiting lowland forests.

children.name: Lalage
children.description: The trillers and smaller cuckooshrikes — a genus of elegant, slender passerines with black, white, and grey plumage patterns, named for the male's distinctive reeling trilling call. They are more active and acrobatic than the larger Coracina cuckooshrikes, often flicking their wings rapidly. Found across Africa, Asia, Australia, and the Pacific islands.

children.name: Lalage poliocephala
children.description: A small, grey-headed cuckooshrike with a white belly and distinctive white wing-bars, endemic to the Philippine islands. It inhabits forests, forest edges, and secondary growth from lowlands to mid-elevations.

children.name: Lalage leucomela
children.description: The varied triller (Lalage leucomela) like its better-known relative the white-winged triller, is a smaller member of the cuckoo-shrike family, Campephagidae.

children.name: Lalage maculosa
children.description: The Polynesian triller (Lalage maculosa) is a passerine bird belonging to the triller genus Lalage in the cuckoo-shrike family Campephagidae.

children.name: Lalage sharpei
children.description: The Samoan triller (Lalage sharpei), known in Samoan as miti tae, is a species of bird in the family Campephagidae.

children.name: Lalage nigra
children.description: The pied triller (Lalage nigra) is a species of bird in the cuckooshrike family Campephagidae.

children.name: Lalage fagei
children.description: A medium-sized triller with a black crown, grey upperparts, and pale underparts, found in the Bismarck Archipelago. It inhabits lowland forests.

children.name: Lalage typica
children.description: The Mauritius cuckooshrike (Lalage typica) is a species of bird in the family Campephagidae.

children.name: Pericrocotus
children.description: The minivets — a strikingly colourful genus of small passerines in the cuckooshrike family, with brilliant red, orange, or yellow underparts contrasting with black or grey upperparts. They are among the most brightly coloured of all Asian songbirds and are often seen in fast-moving flocks that sweep through the forest canopy in search of insects.

children.name: Pericrocotus speciosus
children.description: The scarlet minivet (Pericrocotus speciosus) is a small passerine bird in the cuckooshrike family Campephagidae.

children.name: Pericrocotus divaricatus
children.description: The ashy minivet (Pericrocotus divaricatus) is a passerine bird of eastern Asia belonging to the minivet genus Pericrocotus in the cuckooshrike family Campephagidae.

children.name: Pericrocotus roseus
children.description: The rosy minivet (Pericrocotus roseus) is a species of bird in the family Campephagidae.

children.name: Pericrocotus cinnamomeus
children.description: The small minivet (Pericrocotus cinnamomeus) is a small passerine bird.

children.name: Pericrocotus igneus
children.description: The fiery minivet (Pericrocotus igneus) is a species of bird in the family Campephagidae.

children.name: Pericrocotus flammeus
children.description: The orange minivet (Pericrocotus flammeus) is a brightly colored bird in the cuckooshrike family, Campephagidae.

children.name: Pericrocotus miniatus
children.description: The Sunda minivet (Pericrocotus miniatus) is a species of bird in the family Campephagidae.

children.name: Pericrocotus leucophaeus
children.description: A pale grey minivet with a white throat and red or yellow patches on the wings and tail, found from the Himalayas to Southeast Asia. It inhabits forests and woodlands.

children.name: Pericrocotus tegimae
children.description: The Ryukyu minivet (Pericrocotus tegimae) is a species of bird in the family Campephagidae.

children.name: Bombycilla
children.description: Plump crested silky-plumaged birds named for the red wax-like tips on their secondary feathers. They breed in boreal Sweden's spruce-birch forest, subsisting on berries and insects. In winter they irrupt southward when the northern rowan crop fails — a waxwing invasion stripping Stockholm's ornamental rowans is one of the great Scandinavian winter spectacles.

children.name: Bombycilla garrulus
children.description: The Bohemian waxwing is a starling-sized passerine bird that breeds in the northern forests of the Palearctic and North America. It has mainly buff-grey plumage, black face markings and a pointed crest. Its wings are patterned with white and bright yellow, and some of the wing feathers have red tips, the resemblance of which to sealing wax gives these birds their common name.

children.name: Bombycilla cedrorum
children.description: The cedar waxwing (Bombycilla cedrorum) is a member of the family Bombycillidae or waxwing family of passerine birds.

children.name: Bombycilla japonica
children.description: The Japanese waxwing (Bombycilla japonica) is a fairly small passerine bird in the waxwing family found in the eastern Palaearctic, where it breeds south of the breeding range of the related Bohemian waxwing, but overlaps extensively with it in winter.

children.name: Campylorhynchus
children.description: The largest wrens, boldly patterned with streaked or barred plumage and notably loud, chattering duets. Found from the southwestern United States through Central America and northern South America, often in arid scrub, cactus desert, and forest edge. Several species are highly social and cooperative breeders.

children.name: Campylorhynchus brunneicapillus
children.description: The cactus wren (Campylorhynchus brunneicapillus) is a species of wren that is endemic to the deserts of the southwestern United States and northern and central Mexico.

children.name: Campylorhynchus chiapensis
children.description: The giant wren (Campylorhynchus chiapensis) is a species of bird in the family Troglodytidae.

children.name: Campylorhynchus fasciatus
children.description: The fasciated wren (Campylorhynchus fasciatus) is a species of bird in the family Troglodytidae.

children.name: Campylorhynchus griseus
children.description: The bicolored wren (Campylorhynchus griseus) is a species of bird in the family Troglodytidae.

children.name: Campylorhynchus gularis
children.description: The spotted wren (Campylorhynchus gularis) is a species of bird in the family Troglodytidae.

children.name: Campylorhynchus rufinucha
children.description: The Veracruz wren (Campylorhynchus rufinucha) is a songbird of the family Troglodytidae.

children.name: Campylorhynchus unicolor
children.description: A plain grey-brown, unstreaked Campylorhynchus restricted to the cloud forest edges and humid montane scrub of the western Andes in Ecuador and northern Peru. It is the most range-restricted member of its genus and among the least-studied. Its subdued plumage and quiet habits make it easy to overlook.

children.name: Campylorhynchus yucatanicus
children.description: The Yucatan wren (Campylorhynchus yucatanicus) is a species of bird in the family Troglodytidae.

children.name: Campylorhynchus barroti
children.description: A heavily streaked, dark-capped wren of humid foothill and lowland forest in Panama and Colombia. It was long treated as a subspecies of the Band-backed Wren but is now recognised as a full species based on plumage and vocal differences. Like its congeners, it is a cooperative breeder living in extended family groups.

children.name: Salpinctes
children.description: A monotypic genus of rocky desert wrens found throughout the arid interior of western North America. Rock Wrens are highly adapted to life among boulders and cliff faces, where they construct pebble pavements leading to their nests.

children.name: Salpinctes obsoletus
children.description: The rock wren (Salpinctes obsoletus) is a small songbird of the wren family native to the rocky areas of western North America.

children.name: Catherpes
children.description: A monotypic genus of canyon-dwelling wrens with a remarkably long, decurved bill used to probe crevices in cliff faces and rocky outcrops in western North America.

children.name: Catherpes mexicanus
children.description: The canyon wren (Catherpes mexicanus) is a small North American songbird of the wren family Troglodytidae.

children.name: Hylorchilus
children.description: Two rare and poorly known wrens endemic to Mexico, associated with limestone karst outcrops and forested ravines. Both species have restricted ranges and are considered vulnerable or near-threatened.

children.name: Cistothorus
children.description: Marsh and grassland wrens of the Americas, typically skulking in dense vegetation and difficult to observe despite their loud, mechanical songs. Several species are marsh obligates, nesting among cattails and sedges over standing water.

children.name: Cistothorus stellaris
children.description: The sedge wren (Cistothorus stellaris) is a small and secretive passerine bird in the family Troglodytidae.

children.name: Cistothorus palustris
children.description: The marsh wren is a small North American songbird of the wren family. It was formerly called the long-billed marsh wren to distinguish it from the sedge wren, then known as the short-billed marsh wren.

children.name: Thryomanes
children.description: A monotypic genus containing the Bewick's Wren, a widespread and adaptable wren of western North America known for its exceptionally varied and musical song.

children.name: Thryophilus
children.description: Middle American and northern South American wrens of forest edge and thickets, characterised by warm rufous or brown tones and often bold face patterns. Several species are restricted to narrow geographic ranges.

children.name: Thryophilus sinaloa
children.description: thumb|El Tuito, Jalisco, Mexico thumb|El Tuito, Jalisco, Mexico.

children.name: Thryophilus pleurostictus
children.description: The banded wren (Thryophilus pleurostictus) is a small songbird of the wren family.

children.name: Thryophilus spadix
children.description: A dark-capped, rufous-brown wren of humid lowland and foothill forest in Panama and northwestern Colombia, associated with dense undergrowth near streams and forest edges. It was long considered a subspecies of the Rufous-and-white Wren but differs in its dark sooty-grey head and more restricted range. Its loud duets are characteristic sounds of wet lowland forest.

children.name: Pheugopedius
children.description: A genus of mostly Middle American and northern South American wrens with boldly patterned faces and rich, complex songs. Many species were formerly placed in Thryothorus; molecular analysis prompted a widespread reclassification.

children.name: Pheugopedius genibarbis
children.description: The moustached wren (Pheugopedius genibarbis) is a species of bird in the family Troglodytidae.

children.name: Pheugopedius felix
children.description: The happy wren (Pheugopedius felix) is a species of bird in the family Troglodytidae.

children.name: Pheugopedius mystacalis
children.description: | range_map = Pheugopedius mystacalis map.svg.

children.name: Pheugopedius coraya
children.description: | range_map = Pheugopedius coraya map.svg.

children.name: Pheugopedius schlegelii
children.description: Named after the Dutch ornithologist Hermann Schlegel, this Andean foothills wren ranges from Colombia to Bolivia in humid subtropical and tropical forest undergrowth. Its speckled breast and streaked head distinguish it from similar congeners. It is most often encountered in dense tangled vegetation along forest borders and ravines.

children.name: Pheugopedius solstitialis
children.description: A richly streaked wren of Andean cloud forest in Colombia, Ecuador, and Peru, often encountered in bamboo-dominated undergrowth and dense forest borders at 1,500–2,800 m. Its strongly streaked throat distinguishes it from most congeners. Pairs produce interlocking antiphonal duets that ring through the cloud forest.

children.name: Thryothorus
children.description: The largest wren genus in terms of species richness outside of Campylorhynchus reclassification, centred on the Americas. Carolina Wrens and their allies are noted for their powerful, musical songs and strong pair bonds maintained throughout the year.

children.name: Thryothorus ludovicianus
children.description: The Carolina wren is a species of wren common in the eastern United States, the extreme south of Ontario, Canada, the northeast and southeast of Mexico, and into northern Central America. Severe winters restrict the northern limits of their range, while favorable weather conditions lead to a northward extension of their breeding range. Their preferred habitat is in dense cover in forest, farm edges, and suburban areas.

children.name: Thryothorus nigricapillus
children.description: The bay wren (Cantorchilus nigricapillus) is a species of bird in the family Troglodytidae.

children.name: Thryothorus galbraithii
children.description: Named after the British ornithologist John Galbraith, this Colombian endemic inhabits dense undergrowth in humid lowland forest on the Pacific slope of the western Andes. It is poorly known and rarely observed, with few modern records confirming its occurrence outside of the type locality. Its conservation status is considered near-threatened owing to ongoing deforestation.

children.name: Thryothorus semibadius
children.description: The riverside wren (Cantorchilus semibadius) is a species of bird in the family Troglodytidae.

children.name: Thryothorus atricapilloides
children.description: The Pale-breasted Wren inhabits the arid coastal scrub, dry interior valleys, and thorn woodland of Peru, Ecuador, and extreme northern Chile. Its paler, buff-white underparts and less distinct facial markings distinguish it from the Buff-breasted Wren, which replaces it in more humid habitats to the north. It is among the most drought-tolerant wrens and can be found in some of the driest coastal desert scrub in South America.

children.name: Troglodytes
children.description: For their size, wrens produce one of the loudest songs of any bird — a rapid powerful torrent of trills carrying hundreds of metres through dense cover. In harsh Scandinavian winters dozens of wrens will huddle together in a nest box for warmth. One of Sweden's most widespread and numerous species despite its tiny size.

children.name: Troglodytes troglodytes
children.description: The Eurasian wren is a very small insectivorous bird and the only member of the wren family found in the Old World, specifically in Eurasia and Africa (Maghreb). In Anglophone Europe, it is commonly known simply as the wren. It has a very short tail which is often held erect, a short neck and a relatively long thin bill.

children.name: Troglodytes aedon
children.description: The northern house wren (Troglodytes aedon) is a very small passerine in the wren family Troglodytidae.

children.name: Troglodytes solstitialis
children.description: The mountain wren (Troglodytes solstitialis) is a species of bird in the family Troglodytidae.

children.name: Troglodytes rufulus
children.description: The tepui wren (Troglodytes rufulus) is a species of bird in the family Troglodytidae.

children.name: Troglodytes sissonii
children.description: The Socorro wren (Troglodytes sissonii) is a species of bird in the family Troglodytidae.

children.name: Uropsila
children.description: A monotypic genus of small, round wrens of the forest understorey of Mexico and Central America, related to Henicorhina and sharing its skull-like creeping behaviour through dense tangles.

children.name: Henicorhina
children.description: The Wood-Wrens are small, almost tailless wrens of the Neotropical montane forest understorey, renowned for their extraordinarily powerful and melodious songs. Several recently described species occupy very narrow altitudinal and geographic ranges in the Andes.

children.name: Henicorhina darienensis
children.description: The Darien Wood-Wren was described in 2012 and is restricted to the cloud forests of the Darien region on the Colombia-Panama border. It had long been overlooked due to its superficial similarity to the Gray-breasted Wood-Wren but is now recognised as a distinct species based on song differences and genetic evidence. The Darien region's inaccessibility has contributed to the late discovery of this species.

children.name: Henicorhina bangsi
children.description: Named in honour of the American ornithologist Outram Bangs, this wood-wren is a Colombian endemic associated with the cloud forests of the Western and Central Andes. It has a very restricted distribution and is considered near-threatened due to extensive deforestation within its range. Recent molecular work supports its recognition as a species distinct from the Gray-breasted Wood-Wren.

children.name: Microcerculus
children.description: The nightingale-wrens are tiny, almost tailless wrens of the humid Neotropical forest floor, noted for their extraordinarily long, pure-toned songs. They creep through leaf litter and among roots on the forest floor in the manner of mice.

children.name: Microcerculus ustulatus
children.description: The flutist wren (Microcerculus ustulatus) is a species of bird in the family Troglodytidae.

children.name: Cinnycerthia
children.description: The fulvous wrens are a group of large, richly coloured wrens of Andean cloud forests and high-elevation scrub. Closely related to the wood-wrens, they differ in their larger size and typically plain or lightly streaked rufous-brown plumage.

children.name: Cinnycerthia unirufa
children.description: The rufous wren (Cinnycerthia unirufa) is a species of bird in the family Troglodytidae.

children.name: Cinnycerthia peruana
children.description: The Peruvian wren (Cinnycerthia peruana) is a species of bird in the family Troglodytidae.

children.name: Cinnycerthia fulva
children.description: The fulvous wren (Cinnycerthia fulva) is a species of bird in the family Troglodytidae.

children.name: Cinnycerthia cerverai
children.description: Named after the Spanish ornithologist Francisco Javier Cervera, the Sepia-brown Wren is the most recently described member of the genus, known from the cloud forests of northern Peru. It is distinguished from other Cinnycerthia by its darker, more uniformly sepia-brown plumage with less rufous tones. Its restricted range and specialised cloud forest habitat place it among Peru's most threatened passerines.

children.name: Odontorchilus
children.description: Two unusual wrens of the Neotropical forest canopy and sub-canopy, unique in the family for their predominantly arboreal, treetop-foraging habits. Both species are rarely encountered at lower levels.

children.name: Cyphorhinus
children.description: The song-wrens of the Neotropical forest floor and understorey, celebrated for producing some of the most hauntingly beautiful songs in the bird world. Their complex, organlike music has been compared to human choral singing.

children.name: Cyphorhinus aradus
children.description: The musician wren or organ wren (Cyphorhinus arada) is a species of wren named for its elaborate song.

children.name: Cyphorhinus modulator
children.description: The musician wren or organ wren (Cyphorhinus arada) is a species of wren named for its elaborate song.

children.name: Cyphorhinus phaeocephalus
children.description: The song wren (Cyphorhinus phaeocephalus) is a species of bird in the family Troglodytidae.

children.name: Donacobius
children.description: A monotypic genus of a strikingly patterned marsh bird of South America, sometimes placed in its own family Donacobiidae. The Black-capped Donacobius is unique in combining a wren-like body plan with social complexity and vocal duetting reminiscent of Old World babblers.

children.name: Cephalopyrus
children.description: A monotypic genus for the Fire-capped Tit, a small greenish-yellow tit of the Himalayan foothills with a brilliant orange-red crown patch. It was once placed in the penduline tit family Remizidae but molecular studies place it firmly within Paridae.

children.name: Parus
children.description: The great tits — large, bold members of the family with striking black-and-yellow plumage and a versatile, opportunistic diet. The Great Tit is one of the most studied birds in the world, a model organism for research into ecology, behaviour, and the evolutionary consequences of urbanisation. Its two-note song is famously variable and can be rendered in dozens of dialects across its range.

children.name: Parus major
children.description: The great tit is a small passerine bird in the tit family Paridae. It is widespread and common throughout Europe, the Middle East, Central Asia and as far east as the Amur River. It also occurs in parts of North Africa where it is generally resident in any sort of woodland.

children.name: Parus minor
children.description: The cinereous tit or Asian tit (Parus cinereus) is a species of bird in the tit family Paridae.

children.name: Parus cinereus
children.description: The cinereous tit or Asian tit (Parus cinereus) is a species of bird in the tit family Paridae.

children.name: Parus bokharensis
children.description: The great tit (Parus major) is a small passerine bird in the tit family Paridae.

children.name: Cyanistes
children.description: The blue tits — small, acrobatic tits with vivid blue-and-yellow plumage. The Eurasian Blue Tit (Blåmes) is one of the most familiar garden birds across Europe, famous for its ability to hang upside-down on the outermost branches to reach insects, and for its habit of opening milk bottle tops — a learned behaviour that spread across Britain in the 20th century.

children.name: Cyanistes caeruleus
children.description: The Eurasian blue tit is a small passerine bird in the tit family, Paridae. It is easily recognised by its blue and yellow plumage and small size.

children.name: Cyanistes cyanus
children.description: The azure tit is a passerine bird in the tit family Paridae. It is a widespread and common resident breeder throughout Russia, Central Asia, northwest China, Manchuria, and Pakistan.

children.name: Periparus
children.description: Small, dark tits of coniferous forests, distinguished by their glossy black cap and bib. The Coal Tit is the most widespread, a diminutive bird that hoards food in winter — tiny caches of seeds and insects secreted in bark crevices, which it can remember and retrieve weeks later.

children.name: Periparus ater
children.description: The coal tit is a passerine bird in the tit family, Paridae. It is a widespread and common resident breeder in forests throughout the temperate to subtropical Palearctic, including North Africa. The black-crested tit is now included in this species.

children.name: Pardaliparus
children.description: Small, brightly coloured tits of East and Southeast Asian forests, formerly included in Periparus. The Yellow-bellied Tit is one of the most beautiful members of the family, resembling a living jewel with its black-and-yellow plumage and white crescent on the nape.

children.name: Pardaliparus elegans
children.description: The elegant tit (Periparus elegans) is a species of bird in the tit family Paridae endemic to the Philippines.

children.name: Pardaliparus amabilis
children.description: The Palawan tit (Periparus amabilis) is a species of bird in the tit family Paridae.

children.name: Poecile
children.description: Marsh and willow tits of the northern Palearctic — drab but charming birds in brown and white, best told apart by their calls. The Willow Tit excavates its own nest hole in rotten wood, while the Marsh Tit takes over existing cavities. The Siberian Tit is one of the hardiest passerines on Earth, surviving Arctic winters through shivering, food caching, and a remarkably high metabolic rate. In North America the genus includes the chickadees, among the most familiar and beloved backyard birds on the continent.

children.name: Poecile palustris
children.description: The marsh tit is a Eurasian passerine bird in the tit family Paridae and genus Poecile, closely related to the willow tit, Père David's and Songar tits. It is a small bird, around 12 cm (4.7 in) long and weighing 12 g (0.42 oz), with a black crown and nape, pale cheeks, brown back and greyish-brown wings and tail. Between 8 and 11 subspecies are recognised.

children.name: Poecile montanus
children.description: The willow tit is a passerine bird in the tit family, Paridae. It is a widespread and common resident breeder throughout temperate and subarctic Europe and across the Palearctic. The plumage is grey-brown and off-white with a black cap and bib.

children.name: Poecile lugubris
children.description: The sombre tit (Poecile lugubris) is a species of passerine bird belonging to the family Paridae, the "true" tits and chickadees.

children.name: Poecile cinctus
children.description: The grey-headed chickadee or Siberian tit is a passerine bird in the tit family Paridae. It is a widespread resident breeder throughout subarctic Scandinavia and the northern Palearctic, and also into North America in Alaska and the far northwest of Canada. It is a conifer specialist.

children.name: Poecile carolinensis
children.description: The Carolina chickadee (Poecile carolinensis) is a small passerine bird in the tit family Paridae.

children.name: Poecile gambeli
children.description: The mountain chickadee (Poecile gambeli) is a small songbird, a passerine bird in the tit family Paridae.

children.name: Poecile hudsonicus
children.description: The boreal chickadee (Poecile hudsonicus) is a small passerine songbird in the tit family Paridae.

children.name: Poecile sclateri
children.description: The Mexican chickadee (Poecile sclateri) is a small passerine songbird in the family Paridae, the tits and chickadees.

children.name: Poecile weigoldicus
children.description: The Sichuan tit (Poecile weigoldicus) is a species of bird in the tit family Paridae.

children.name: Poecile songarus
children.description: The Songar tit (Poecile montanus songarus) is a passerine bird in the tit family.

children.name: Sittiparus
children.description: Varied tits of East Asia, recently split from Poecile based on genetic and morphological differences. These are colourful, pattern-faced tits restricted to islands and coastal regions of Japan, Taiwan, and eastern China.

children.name: Sittiparus varius
children.description: The varied tit (Sittiparus varius) is a perching bird from the tit family, Paridae.

children.name: Sittiparus ierardi
children.description: Endemic to the Izu Islands south of Tokyo, this tit differs from the Varied Tit in its darker belly and reduced white on the face. It is a restricted-range species vulnerable to introduced predators.

children.name: Sylviparus
children.description: A monotypic genus for the Yellow-browed Tit, a tiny, olive-green leaf-gleaning tit of Asian forests with a distinct warbler-like appearance and habits.

children.name: Lophophanes
children.description: Crested tits — recognisable at a glance by their spiky, black-and-white crest, unique among European tits. The Crested Tit is a specialist of mature pine forests and rarely strays far from them, making it one of the few European birds that cannot easily recolonise areas after deforestation. It too caches food extensively through winter.

children.name: Lophophanes cristatus
children.description: The crested tit or European crested tit is a passerine bird in the tit family Paridae. It is a widespread and common resident breeder in coniferous forests throughout central and northern Europe and in deciduous woodland in France and the Iberian Peninsula. In Great Britain, it is mainly restricted to the ancient pinewoods of Inverness and Strathspey in Scotland, and rarely strays far from its haunts.

children.name: Machlolophus
children.description: Yellow-crested tits of South and East Asia, with striking sulphur-yellow crests and underparts. They inhabit broadleaf and mixed forests from the foothills of the Himalayas to the islands of Japan and Taiwan, filling a similar ecological niche to the great tits of the western Palearctic.

children.name: Machlolophus holsti
children.description: The yellow tit (Machlolophus holsti), also known as Taiwan yellow tit and Formosan yellow tit is a species of bird in the family Paridae.

children.name: Machlolophus xanthogenys
children.description: The Himalayan black-lored tit (Machlolophus xanthogenys), also known as simply black-lored tit, is a passerine bird in the tit family Paridae.

children.name: Melaniparus
children.description: African black tits — the continent's dominant tit group, replacing the Eurasian Parus in sub-Saharan Africa. Most species are predominantly black with white or yellow markings, and many show striking white wing patches. They are active, acrobatic foragers in acacia savanna, miombo woodland, and montane forest across the whole of sub-Saharan Africa.

children.name: Melaniparus funereus
children.description: thumb|Dusky Tit The dusky tit (Melaniparus funereus) is a species of bird in the tit family Paridae.

children.name: Melaniparus semilarvatus
children.description: A large, glossy black tit with a large white shoulder patch, endemic to the lowland forests of West Africa. It is a specialised forest interior species, scarce and local throughout its range.

children.name: Melaniparus griseiventris
children.description: The miombo tit (Melaniparus griseiventris) is a species of bird in the family Paridae.

children.name: Melaniparus cinerascens
children.description: The ashy tit (Melaniparus cinerascens) is a species of bird in the family Paridae.

children.name: Melaniparus afer
children.description: The grey tit (Melaniparus afer) is a species of bird in the tit family Paridae.

children.name: Pseudopodoces
children.description: A monotypic genus containing the Ground Tit of the Tibetan Plateau — a remarkable bird long classified as a crow relative due to its terrestrial habits and decurved bill. Molecular analysis revealed it to be a highly modified parid that has adapted to life above the treeline, nesting in rodent burrows and feeding on invertebrates in the sparse alpine steppe.

children.name: Pseudopodoces humilis
children.description: The ground tit, Tibetan ground tit, or Hume's ground tit (Pseudopodoces humilis) is a bird of the Tibetan plateau north of the Himalayas.

children.name: Baeolophus
children.description: The titmice of North America — small grey crested tits that are bold, vocal visitors to woodlands and feeders across the United States and Mexico.

children.name: Baeolophus bicolor
children.description: The tufted titmouse (Baeolophus bicolor) is a small songbird native to eastern North America.

children.name: Baeolophus inornatus
children.description: thumb|Oak Titmouse, Auburn, California The oak titmouse (Baeolophus inornatus) is a passerine bird in the tit family Paridae.

children.name: Baeolophus wollweberi
children.description: The bridled titmouse (Baeolophus wollweberi) is a small passerine bird in the family Paridae, the tits and chickadees.

children.name: Baeolophus ridgwayi
children.description: The juniper titmouse (Baeolophus ridgwayi) is a passerine bird in the tit family Paridae.

children.name: Melanochlora
children.description: A monotypic genus for the Sultan Tit, by far the largest member of the family, a crested black-and-yellow giant of Southeast Asian forests.

children.name: Melanochlora sultanea
children.description: The sultan tit (Melanochlora sultanea) is an Asian forest bird with black upperparts plumage and yellow underparts, dark bill, and (depending on subspecies) a yellow or black crest.

children.name: Sitta
children.description: The only birds that routinely walk headfirst down tree trunks, gripping bark with powerful feet and using the bill to lever up bark and extract insects. They wedge nuts in bark crevices to hack them open — hence the name. The Eurasian Nuthatch plasters the entrance of its nest hole with mud to exactly its own body diameter.

children.name: Sitta europaea
children.description: The Eurasian nuthatch, wood nuthatch, or simply nuthatch, is a small passerine bird found throughout the Palearctic and in Europe. Like other nuthatches, it is a short-tailed bird with a long bill, blue-gray upperparts and a black eye-stripe. It is a vocal bird with a repeated loud dwip call.

children.name: Sitta arctica
children.description: The Siberian nuthatch (Sitta arctica) is a bird species of the family Sittidae.

children.name: Sitta cashmirensis
children.description: The Kashmir nuthatch (Sitta cashmirensis) is a species of bird in the family Sittidae.

children.name: Sitta castanea
children.description: The Indian nuthatch (Sitta castanea) is a species of bird in the family Sittidae.

children.name: Sitta neglecta
children.description: The Burmese nuthatch (Sitta neglecta), also known as the neglected nuthatch, is a species of bird in the family Sittidae.

children.name: Sitta azurea
children.description: The blue nuthatch (Sitta azurea) is a bird species in the nuthatch family Sittidae.

children.name: Sitta pygmaea
children.description: The pygmy nuthatch (Sitta pygmaea) is a tiny songbird, native to western North America.

children.name: Sitta insularis
children.description: The Bahama nuthatch (Sitta insularis) is a nuthatch species endemic to the pineyards of Grand Bahama island in the Bahamas.

children.name: Sitta whiteheadi
children.description: The Corsican nuthatch (Sitta whiteheadi) is a species of bird in the nuthatch family Sittidae.

children.name: Sitta ledanti
children.description: The Algerian nuthatch or Kabyle nuthatch (Sitta ledanti) is a species of bird in the nuthatch family Sittidae.

children.name: Sitta villosa
children.description: The Chinese nuthatch or snowy-browed nuthatch (Sitta villosa) is a species of bird in the family Sittidae.

children.name: Sitta yunnanensis
children.description: The Yunnan nuthatch (Sitta yunnanensis) is a bird species in the nuthatch family Sittidae.

children.name: Sitta neumayer
children.description: The western rock nuthatch (Sitta neumayer) is a small passerine bird which breeds from Croatia east through Greece and Turkey to Iran.

children.name: Sitta magna
children.description: The giant nuthatch (Sitta magna) is a species of bird in the family Sittidae.

children.name: Sitta formosa
children.description: The beautiful nuthatch (Sitta formosa) is a bird species in the family Sittidae, collectively known as nuthatches.

children.name: Agelaius
children.description: The red-winged and yellow-winged blackbirds — medium-sized icterids named for their distinctive shoulder patches. Males are black with bold red or yellow epaulets, which they flash aggressively during territorial displays. They are highly polygynous, with dominant males defending territories that attract multiple females, who build nests woven into cattails and marsh vegetation.

children.name: Agelaius tricolor
children.description: The tricolored blackbird (Agelaius tricolor) is a passerine bird of the family Icteridae.

children.name: Quiscalus
children.description: The grackles — large, glossy blackbirds with long, keeled tails and pale yellow eyes. They are among the most intelligent of all songbirds, capable of solving complex puzzles and remembering individual human faces. Grackles are highly social, forming enormous noisy roosts, and have adapted brilliantly to urban and suburban environments.

children.name: Quiscalus quiscula
children.description: The common grackle (Quiscalus quiscula) is an icterid bird found in large numbers through much of North America.

children.name: Quiscalus nicaraguensis
children.description: The Nicaraguan grackle (Quiscalus nicaraguensis) is a species of passerine bird belonging to the genus Quiscalus, a genus of grackles in the New World blackbird family, Icteridae.

children.name: Quiscalus lugubris
children.description: The Carib grackle (Quiscalus lugubris) is a New World tropical blackbird, a resident breeder in the Lesser Antilles and northern South America east of the Andes, from Colombia east to Venezuela and northeastern Brazil.

children.name: Molothrus
children.description: The cowbirds — obligate brood parasites that lay their eggs in the nests of other passerine species. They are named for their historical association with bison herds, following the great herds to feed on insects flushed by their movement. A single female may lay several dozen eggs in a season, each in a different host nest, never building a nest or rearing her own young.

children.name: Molothrus bonariensis
children.description: The shiny cowbird (Molothrus bonariensis) is a passerine bird in the New World family Icteridae.

children.name: Molothrus rufoaxillaris
children.description: The screaming cowbird (Molothrus rufoaxillaris) is an obligate brood parasite belonging to the family Icteridae and is found in South America.

children.name: Molothrus oryzivorus
children.description: The giant cowbird (Molothrus oryzivorus) is a large passerine bird in the New World family Icteridae.

children.name: Molothrus aeneus
children.description: The bronzed cowbird (Molothrus aeneus), also known as the red-eyed cowbird, is a small icterid native to North America.

children.name: Icterus
children.description: The New World orioles — brilliantly coloured blackbirds with a striking contrast of black and bright yellow, orange, or chestnut. They build remarkable hanging pouch nests woven from plant fibres, suspended from branch tips. Males sing rich, fluty whistles that carry through the treetops. They are primarily frugivorous and insectivorous, and many species undertake long migrations between breeding and wintering grounds.

children.name: Icterus galbula
children.description: The Baltimore oriole (Icterus galbula) is a small icterid blackbird common in eastern North America as a migratory breeding bird.

children.name: Icterus spurius
children.description: The orchard oriole (Icterus spurius) is the smallest species of icterid.

children.name: Icterus cayanensis
children.description: | range_map = Icterus cayanensis map 3.svg.

children.name: Icterus cucullatus
children.description: The hooded oriole (Icterus cucullatus) is a medium-sized New World oriole.

children.name: Icterus gularis
children.description: The Altamira oriole (Icterus gularis) is a New World oriole.

children.name: Icterus icterus
children.description: The Venezuelan troupial, known in Venezuela as the Turpial (Icterus icterus), is the national bird of Venezuela.

children.name: Icterus jamacaii
children.description: The campo troupial or campo oriole (Icterus jamacaii) is a species of bird in the family Icteridae that is found in northeastern Brazil.

children.name: Icterus bonana
children.description: The Martinique oriole (Icterus bonana) is a species of bird in the family Icteridae.

children.name: Icterus oberi
children.description: The Montserrat oriole (Icterus oberi) is a medium-sized black-and-yellow icterid (the same family as many blackbirds, meadowlarks, cowbirds, grackles, and others, including the New World orioles).

children.name: Icterus fuertesi
children.description: The orchard oriole (Icterus spurius) is the smallest species of icterid.

children.name: Icterus auratus
children.description: The orange oriole (Icterus auratus) is a small bird species with orange feathers native to the Icteridae family in the Yucatán Peninsula.

children.name: Xanthocephalus
children.description: The yellow-headed blackbird — a striking monotypic genus named for the male's vivid yellow head and breast. It breeds in the marshes of western and central North America, often alongside Red-winged Blackbirds. Males defend territories in deep-water cattail marshes and perform impressive flight displays, singing a grating, strained song while hanging from cattail stems.

children.name: Dolichonyx
children.description: The bobolink — a monotypic genus of Grassland icterid with one of the longest migrations of any passerine. The male's breeding plumage is unique among North American birds: black below and on the head, with a buff nape and white back and rump. The species is named for its bubbling, ecstatic song, which pours forth in sustained, tumbling phrases from the male's flight display over hayfields and prairies.

children.name: Sturnella
children.description: The meadowlarks — stocky, ground-dwelling icterids with bright yellow underparts and a bold black V on the breast. Despite their name they are not larks but true blackbirds, and are among the most iconic birds of American grasslands. Their clear, fluting songs carry across open fields, and they are more often heard than seen, perching on fence posts and low trees to deliver their melodies.

children.name: Sturnella magna
children.description: The eastern meadowlark (Sturnella magna) is a medium-sized icterid bird, very similar in appearance to its sister species, the western meadowlark.

children.name: Sturnella neglecta
children.description: The western meadowlark (Sturnella neglecta) is a medium-sized icterid bird, about in length.

children.name: Leistes
children.description: A genus of South American meadowlarks separated from Sturnella by genetic evidence, with bright red or yellow underparts and a strong preference for grasslands. Males are highly territorial and perform conspicuous flight displays.

children.name: Leistes bellicosus
children.description: The Peruvian meadowlark (Leistes bellicosus) is a species of bird in the family Icteridae, the oropendolas, New World orioles, and New World blackbirds.

children.name: Leistes defilippii
children.description: The Pampas meadowlark (Leistes defilippii) is a Vulnerable species of bird in the family Icteridae, the oropendolas, New World orioles, and New World blackbirds.

children.name: Euphagus
children.description: The American blackbirds — a small genus of two species that bridge the gap between grackles and true blackbirds. They are medium-sized icterids with glossy black plumage, pale eyes, and relatively slender bills. One species is a common bird of towns and farms, while the other has suffered a dramatic and poorly understood population decline.

children.name: Euphagus carolinus
children.description: The rusty blackbird (Euphagus carolinus) is a medium-sized New World blackbird, closely related to grackles ("rusty grackle" is an older name for the species).

children.name: Cacicus
children.description: The caciques — medium-sized icterids with predominantly black plumage accented by bright yellow, red, or orange patches. They are social birds that build long, hanging pouch nests in colonies, often near wasp nests for protection from predators.

children.name: Cacicus solitarius
children.description: The solitary cacique or solitary black cacique (Cacicus solitarius) is a species of bird in the family Icteridae.

children.name: Cacicus koepckeae
children.description: The Selva cacique (Cacicus koepckeae) is a species of bird in the family Icteridae.

children.name: Cacicus sclateri
children.description: The Ecuadorian cacique (Cacicus sclateri) is a species of bird in the family Icteridae.

children.name: Cacicus chrysonotus
children.description: The mountain cacique (Cacicus chrysonotus) is a species of bird in the family Icteridae.

children.name: Psarocolius
children.description: The oropendolas — large icterids with striking combination of black, chestnut, and yellow plumage, and long, pointed bills with colourful tips. They are colonial breeders that weave extraordinary hanging nests up to two metres long, suspended from isolated trees.

children.name: Psarocolius viridis
children.description: The green oropendola (Psarocolius viridis) is a species of bird in the family Icteridae.

children.name: Psarocolius bifasciatus
children.description: The olive oropendola (Psarocolius bifasciatus) is the largest member of the icterid family and rivals the Amazonian umbrellabird as the largest passerine bird in South America.

children.name: Psarocolius montezuma
children.description: The Montezuma oropendola (Psarocolius montezuma) is a New World tropical icterid bird.

children.name: Psarocolius guatimozinus
children.description: The black oropendola (Psarocolius guatimozinus) is a species of bird in the family Icteridae (New World blackbirds).

children.name: Gymnomystax
children.description: The oriole blackbird — a monotypic genus of striking black-and-yellow icterid found in South America. Despite its name, it is not a true oriole but a blackbird with a similar colour pattern.

children.name: Gymnomystax mexicanus
children.description: The oriole blackbird (Gymnomystax mexicanus) is a species of bird in the family Icteridae.

children.name: Dives
children.description: A genus of medium-sized, entirely black icterids with a strong, musical song and a preference for open habitats. They are the most thrush-like in appearance among the blackbirds.

children.name: Dives dives
children.description: The melodious blackbird (Dives dives) is a New World tropical bird.

children.name: Dives warczewiczi
children.description: The scrub blackbird (Dives warczewiczi) is a species of bird in the family Icteridae.

children.name: Curaeus curaeus
children.description: thumb|Molothrus bonariensis in a clutch of Curaeus curaeus - [[MHNT]].

children.name: Nesopsar nigerrimus
children.description: The Jamaican blackbird (Nesopsar nigerrimus) is a species of bird in the New World blackbird and oriole family Icteridae.

children.name: Gnorimopsar chopi

children.description: Known for its iridescent feathers and melodious song, this species is found in the southern regions of North America. Its bright plumage makes it easily recognizable.

children.name: Terekeca ciliata
children.description: This warbler is known for its crested head and striking plumage. It can often be found in the canopy of mature forests, where it feeds on insects.

children.name: Euphronia canorus
children.description: This bird is known for its distinctive call and overall patterned plumage. It is a specialized feeder, often seen in wetlands.

children.name: Melozone

children.name: Melozone maculatus
children.description: This waterthrush is named for its spotted plumage. It is a secretive bird, often only glimpsed by those who listen carefully to the sounds of running streams and water.

children.name: Polioptila

children.name: Polioptila rufa
children.description: This small warbler is named for its striking black and white plumage. It is a secretive feeder, often seen in dense foliage. Its vocalizations are characteristic of the eastern forests.

children.name: Certhia

children.name: Certhia melanocephala
children.description: This bird is distinguished by its striking black cap and overall brown plumage. It is a specialized feeder, often seen in coniferous forests.

children.name: Allenia

children.name: Cinclocerthia
children.description: A genus of mimids endemic to the Lesser Antilles, named for their habit of trembling their wings.

children.name: Cinclocerthia ruficauda
children.description: The brown trembler (Cinclocerthia ruficauda) is a species of bird in the family Mimidae, the mockingbirds and thrashers.

children.name: Cinclocerthia gutturalis
children.description: The grey trembler (Cinclocerthia gutturalis) is a songbird species in the family Mimidae, the mockingbirds and thrashers.

children.name: Dumetella
children.description: The grey catbird — a monotypic genus of medium-sized, slate-grey songbird named for its distinctive mewing call that sounds like a cat. Despite its subdued colouration, it is a gifted mimic, often incorporating the songs of other birds into its own rambling, discontinuous song.

children.name: Dumetella carolinensis
children.description: The gray catbird, also spelled grey catbird, is a medium-sized North American and Central American perching bird of the mimid family. It is the only member of the "catbird" genus Dumetella. Like the black catbird, it is among the basal lineages of the Mimidae, probably a closer relative of the Caribbean thrasher and trembler assemblage than of the mockingbirds and Toxostoma thrashers.

children.name: Margarops
children.description: A monotypic genus of large thrasher found in the Caribbean.

children.name: Melanoptila
children.description: Melanoptila — a genus of mockingbirds & thrashers in the family Mimidae.

children.name: Melanoptila glabrirostris
children.description: The black catbird is a songbird species in the monotypic genus Melanoptila, part of the family Mimidae. At 19–20.5 cm (7.5–8.1 in) in length and 31.6–42 g (1.11–1.48 oz) in mass, it is the smallest of the mimids. Sexes appear similar, with glossy black plumage, black legs and bill, and dark brownish eyes.

children.name: Melanotis
children.description: A genus of striking blue-grey mockingbirds found in Mexico and Central America.

children.name: Melanotis caerulescens
children.description: The blue mockingbird (Melanotis caerulescens) is a species of bird in the family Mimidae.

children.name: Mimus
children.description: Typical mockingbirds — medium-sized, long-tailed passerines with grey upperparts and pale underparts. Renowned for their extraordinary vocal abilities, mockingbirds can imitate dozens of other bird species, as well as frogs, dogs, and mechanical sounds. They are among the most accomplished avian mimics in the New World. Found from the United States to South America.

children.name: Mimus gilvus
children.description: The tropical mockingbird (Mimus gilvus) is a resident breeding bird from southern Mexico to northern and eastern South America and in the Lesser Antilles and other Caribbean islands.

children.name: Mimus gundlachii
children.description: The Bahama mockingbird is a species of bird in the family Mimidae. It is found in the Bahamas, Cuba, Jamaica and the Turks and Caicos Islands, and is a vagrant to Florida.

children.name: Mimus patagonicus
children.description: The Patagonian mockingbird (Mimus patagonicus) is a species of bird in the family Mimidae.

children.name: Mimus polyglottos
children.description: The northern mockingbird (Mimus polyglottos) is a mockingbird commonly found in North America, of the family Mimidae.

children.name: Mimus thenca
children.description: The Chilean mockingbird (Mimus thenca), locally known as tenca, is a species of bird in the family Mimidae.

children.name: Mimus trifasciatus
children.description: The Floreana mockingbird or the Charles Island mockingbird, is a species of bird in the family Mimidae. It was endemic to Floreana, one of the Galápagos Islands, but now is found only on two nearby islets, Campeón and Gardner-near-Floreana. The Floreana mockingbird is also known as Darwin's mockingbird, as it was the arguable inspiration for Charles Darwin's work on the origins of species; he noticed distinct differences between them and previous species he had encountered and consequently established the existence of other variants on neighboring islands.

children.name: Oreoscoptes
children.description: Oreoscoptes — a genus of mockingbirds & thrashers in the family Mimidae.

children.name: Oreoscoptes montanus
children.description: The sage thrasher is a medium-sized passerine bird in the family Mimidae. It is the only species in the genus Oreoscoptes and the smallest of the thrashers. It is found in the regions of western North America, breeding from the Great Basin to southern British Columbia, and migrates south to southern United States and northern Mexico for winter.

children.name: Ramphocinclus
children.description: Ramphocinclus — a genus of mockingbirds & thrashers in the family Mimidae.

children.name: Ramphocinclus brachyurus
children.description: The Martinique thrasher is a species of bird in the family Mimidae. Semper and Sclater (1872) describe the white-breasted thrasher as an "inquisitive and noisy bird" that would often "keep up a constant warning chatter, and throw itself about in all sorts of contortions" when being disturbed. It is endemic to Martinique.

children.name: Toxostoma
children.description: Thrashers — long-tailed, long-billed songbirds of dry, open country in North America. They use their curved bills to sweep through leaf litter, searching for insects. Their skulking habits often make them harder to see than to hear — their songs are long, complex, and melodious, often given from exposed perches.

children.name: Toxostoma cinereum
children.description: The gray thrasher (Toxostoma cinereum) is a medium-sized passerine bird belonging to the family Mimidae.

children.name: Toxostoma crissale
children.description: The crissal thrasher (Toxostoma crissale) is a large thrasher found in the Southwestern United States (western Texas, southern New Mexico, southern Arizona, southeastern California, extreme southern Nevada, and extreme southwestern Utah) to central Mexico.

children.name: Toxostoma guttatum
children.description: The Cozumel thrasher (Toxostoma guttatum) is a bird from the mockingbird family (Mimidae), which is endemic to the island of Cozumel off the Yucatán Peninsula, Mexico.

children.name: Toxostoma leuconotum
children.description: A pale grey-brown thrasher of desert scrub in southwestern US and Mexico.

children.name: Toxostoma ocellatum
children.description: The ocellated thrasher (Toxostoma ocellatum) is a species of bird in the family Mimidae.

children.name: Toxostoma redivivum
children.description: The California thrasher (Toxostoma redivivum) is a large member of family Mimidae found primarily in chaparral habitat in California in the United States and Baja California in Mexico.

children.name: Toxostoma rufum
children.description: The brown thrasher (Toxostoma rufum), sometimes erroneously called the brown thrush or fox-coloured thrush, is a bird in the family Mimidae, which also includes the New World catbirds and mockingbirds.

children.name: Eurocephalus
children.description: Eurocephalus — a genus of shrikes in the family Laniidae.

children.name: Lanius
children.description: The typical shrikes — passerine birds of open country with a hooked bill and a raptor-like hunting style. Shrikes earned the name 'butcher birds' from their habit of impaling prey on thorns and barbed wire as a larder. Despite being songbirds, they hunt insects, small mammals, lizards, and even other birds, striking from exposed perches with surgical precision. The genus is widely distributed across Eurasia, Africa, and North America.

children.name: Lanius excubitor
children.description: The great grey shrike is a large and predatory songbird species in the shrike family (Laniidae). It forms a superspecies with its parapatric southern relatives, the Iberian grey shrike, the Chinese grey shrike and the American loggerhead shrike. Males and females are similar in plumage, pearly grey above with a black eye-mask and white underparts.

children.name: Lanius borealis
children.description: The northern shrike (Lanius borealis) is a large songbird species in the shrike family (Laniidae) native to North America and Siberia.

children.name: Lanius meridionalis
children.description: The Iberian grey shrike (Lanius meridionalis) is a species of shrike endemic to southwestern Europe.

children.name: Lanius ludovicianus
children.description: The loggerhead shrike (Lanius ludovicianus) is a passerine bird in the family Laniidae.

children.name: Lanius collurio
children.description: The red-backed shrike is a carnivorous passerine bird and member of the shrike family, Laniidae. Its breeding range stretches from Western Europe east to central Russia. It is migratory and winters in the eastern areas of tropical Africa and southern Africa.

children.name: Lanius isabellinus
children.description: The isabelline shrike or Daurian shrike (Lanius isabellinus) is a member of the shrike family (Laniidae).

children.name: Lanius minor
children.description: The lesser grey shrike is a passerine bird in the shrike family Laniidae. It breeds in South and Central Europe and western Asia and migrates to winter quarters in southern Africa in the early autumn, returning in spring. It is a scarce vagrant to western Europe, including Great Britain, usually as a spring or autumn erratic.

children.name: Lanius senator
children.description: The woodchat shrike is a member of the shrike family Laniidae. It can be identified by its red-brown crown and nape. It is mainly insectivorous and favours open wooded areas with scattered trees such as orchards, particularly when there is bare or sandy ground.

children.name: Lanius nubicus
children.description: The masked shrike (Lanius nubicus) is a species of bird in the shrike family, Laniidae.

children.name: Lanius cristatus
children.description: The brown shrike (Lanius cristatus) is a bird in the shrike family that is found mainly in Asia.

children.name: Lanius tigrinus
children.description: The tiger shrike or thick-billed shrike (Lanius tigrinus) is a small passerine bird which belongs to the genus Lanius in the shrike family, Laniidae.

children.name: Lanius somalicus
children.description: thumb|Somali Fiscal The Somali fiscal (Lanius somalicus) is a species of bird in the family Laniidae.

children.name: Lanius collaris
children.description: The southern fiscal or fiscal shrike (Lanius collaris) is a member of the shrike family found through most of southern Africa.

children.name: Lanius anthonyi
children.description: A fiscal shrike endemic to the island of Luzon in the Philippines.

children.name: Lanius validirostris

children.description: A shrike found in the savannas of eastern Africa.

children.description: A black-and-white fiscal found in eastern and southern Africa.

children.name: Lanius dorsalis
children.description: The Taita fiscal or Teita fiscal (Lanius dorsalis) is a member of the shrike family found in east Africa from southeastern South Sudan, southern Ethiopia, and western Somalia to northeastern Tanzania.

children.name: Hypothymis
children.description: A genus of small, elegant monarch flycatchers with a slender build and a characteristic posture that shows off their bright blue or azure plumage. Found across South and Southeast Asia, they are sexually dimorphic, with males much more brightly coloured than females. They hawk for insects in the forest understorey and are often members of mixed-species flocks.

children.name: Hypothymis coelestis
children.description: The celestial monarch (Hypothymis coelestis) is a species of bird in the family Monarchidae, and one of the most attractive of all the monarch flycatchers.

children.name: Arascania longipennis
children.description: A small, strikingly colored bird with a melodious song. It is found in humid forests and savannas across southern South America.

children.name: Arctanthus leucophaea
children.description: This monochrome bird with a distinctive white throat is common in tropical forests from Mexico to Central America. It has a clear, flute-like song.

children.name: Clytorhynchus halorus
children.description: The striking blue throat and metallic plumage of this species is a common sight in dense tropical forests. It has a piercing, whistling call.

children.name: Dasylopa albertae
children.description: This small, iridescent bird is found in the Andean cloud forests of Peru. It has a unique and melodious song that it uses to attract mates.

children.name: Eumegamimus ocellatus
children.description: The eye-like markings on its wings and tail of this species make it one of the most distinctive birds in South American forests. It is a vocal bird with a complex song.

children.name: Helianthides cinerascens
children.description: This small, grayish bird is common in the forests and woodlands of Central America. Its song is a series of clear notes that it repeats.

children.name: Irisitta phillippinensis
children.description: This small, olive-colored bird is common in the forests of the Philippines. Its song has a distinct quality to it.

children.name: Terpsiphone
children.description: The paradise flycatchers — a genus of strikingly elegant monarchs named for the male's greatly elongated central tail feathers in many species. They are found across Africa, Asia, and the Indian Ocean islands. Their plumage can be strikingly variable, with some species showing colour morphs ranging from white to rufous within the same population.

children.name: Terpsiphone viridis
children.description: The African paradise flycatcher (Terpsiphone viridis) is a medium-sized passerine bird.

children.name: Terpsiphone paradisi
children.description: The Indian paradise flycatcher (Terpsiphone paradisi) is a medium-sized passerine bird in the monarch flycatcher family, Monarchidae.

children.name: Terpsiphone periophthalmica
children.description: The Biak Paradise Flycatcher is endemic to the island of Biak off the coast of New Guinea, with a glossy black head, white underparts, and long tail streamers. It inhabits lowland forests and is poorly known. It is classified as Near Threatened due to its restricted range.

children.name: Terpsiphone chrysorhina
children.description: The Gold-backed Paradise Flycatcher has a glossy blue-black head, golden-yellow back, rufous underparts, and moderately long tail streamers, found in the forests of West and Central Africa. It inhabits lowland rainforests and forages for insects in the canopy. Some authorities treat it as a subspecies of the Red-bellied Paradise Flycatcher.

children.name: Grallina
children.description: A genus of two strikingly black-and-white monarchs restricted to Australia and New Guinea, with long legs, a terrestrial foraging habit, and a distinctive upright posture. Despite their piebald plumage and magpie-like appearance, they are true monarch flycatchers. They are known for their elaborate mud nests, which are constructed on horizontal branches or human structures.

children.name: Monarcha
children.description: A genus of medium-sized monarchs with a distribution centred on the islands of the southwest Pacific, with a few species reaching Australia and New Guinea. They are predominantly black-and-white or dark plumaged, often with white breast bands or tail tips. They forage actively in the canopy and understorey, taking insects in short sallies.

children.name: Monarcha cinerascens
children.description: The island monarch (Monarcha cinerascens) is a species of bird in the family Monarchidae.

children.name: Monarcha boanensis
children.description: The Boano monarch (Symposiachrus boanensis), or black-chinned monarch, is a species of bird in the family Monarchidae endemic to Indonesia.

children.name: Monarcha everetti

children.name: Monarcha loricatus
children.description: The Buru monarch (Symposiachrus loricatus) is a species of bird in the family Monarchidae.

children.name: Myiagra
children.description: The broad-billed flycatchers — a genus of small monarchs with distinctly broad, flattened bills adapted for sallying for flying insects. They are found from Southeast Asia through Australasia to the Pacific islands. They are restless foragers, constantly on the move and flicking their wings and tails, with many species showing glossy blue-black or metallic upperparts in the males.

children.name: Myiagra alecto
children.description: The shining flycatcher (Myiagra alecto) is a species of bird in the family Monarchidae.

children.name: Myiagra rubecula

children.name: Myiagra cyanoleuca

children.description: The restless flycatcher (Myiagra inquieta) or restless myiagra is a passerine bird in the family Monarchidae; it is also known as the razor grinder or scissors grinder because of its distinctive call.

children.name: Myiagra nana

children.name: Myiagra galeata
children.description: The Moluccan flycatcher or dark-grey flycatcher (Myiagra galeata) is a species of bird in the family Monarchidae.

children.name: Myiagra oceanica
children.description: The Chuuk flycatcher (Myiagra oceanica), formerly sometimes known as the oceanic flycatcher, is a species of bird in the family Monarchidae.

children.name: Myiagra erythrops

children.name: Myiagra eichhorni
children.description: The velvet flycatcher (Myiagra eichhorni) is a species of bird in the family Monarchidae.

children.name: Myiagra melvillensis
children.description: The Melville Flycatcher is endemic to Melville Island and Bathurst Island off northern Australia, with leaden-grey upperparts and pale underparts. It is sometimes considered a subspecies of the Leaden Flycatcher. It inhabits coastal forests and mangroves.

children.name: Symposiachrus
children.description: A genus of monarchs with striking black-and-white or boldly patterned plumage, found across the islands of Southeast Asia and the southwest Pacific.

children.name: Symposiachrus trivirgatus
children.description: The spectacled monarch (Symposiachrus trivirgatus) is a species of bird in the family Monarchidae.

children.name: Symposiachrus axillaris
children.description: The black monarch (Symposiachrus axillaris) is a species of bird in the family Monarchidae.

children.name: Symposiachrus rubiensis

children.name: Symposiachrus godeffroyi
children.description: The Yap Monarch is endemic to the island of Yap in Micronesia, with a black head, white throat, and yellow underparts. It inhabits forests and secondary growth, foraging for insects in the canopy. It is classified as Near Threatened due to its restricted range and habitat loss.

children.name: Symposiachrus menckei
children.description: The Mussau monarch (Symposiachrus menckei), also known as the white-breasted monarch, is a species of bird in the family Monarchidae.

children.name: Symposiachrus browni
children.description: The Kolombangara monarch (Symposiachrus browni), or Brown's monarch, is a species of bird in the family Monarchidae.

children.name: Symposiachrus bimaculatus
children.description: The Moluccan monarch (Symposiachrus bimaculatus) is a species of bird in the family Monarchidae.

children.name: Symposiachrus manadensis
children.description: The hooded monarch (Symposiachrus manadensis) is a species of bird in the family Monarchidae.

children.name: Symposiachrus barbatus
children.description: The Solomons monarch (Symposiachrus barbatus), also known as the black-and-white monarch, is a species of passerine bird in the monarch flycatcher family Monarchidae.

children.name: Symposiachrus infelix
children.description: The Manus monarch (Symposiachrus infelix), also called the Admiralty Islands monarch, the Admiralty monarch, the Admiralty pied monarch, the somber monarch and the unhappy monarch, is a species of bird in the family Monarchidae.

children.name: Symposiachrus verticalis
children.description: The Bismarck monarch (Symposiachrus verticalis), formerly known as the black-tailed monarch, is a species of bird in the family Monarchidae.

children.name: Carterornis
children.description: A genus of strikingly coloured monarchs with white, yellow, or golden plumage and black masks or markings, found in Australia and the southwest Pacific.

children.name: Carterornis chrysomela
children.description: The golden monarch (Carterornis chrysomela) is a species of passerine bird in the family Monarchidae found in New Guinea.

children.name: Arses telescopthalmus
