children.name: Clytorhynchus
children.description: A genus of monarchs known as shrikebills, named for their stout, hooked bills adapted for tearing bark and searching for insects. They are found on islands of the southwest Pacific.

children.name: Clytorhynchus pachycephaloides
children.description: The southern shrikebill (Clytorhynchus pachycephaloides), or brown flycatcher, is a songbird species in the family Monarchidae.

children.name: Clytorhynchus vitiensis
children.description: The Fiji shrikebill (Clytorhynchus vitiensis) is a songbird species in the family Monarchidae.

children.name: Clytorhynchus hamlini
children.description: The Rennell shrikebill (Clytorhynchus hamlini) is a songbird species in the family Monarchidae.

children.name: Metabolus

children.name: Anthreptes griseigularis
children.description: The grey-throated sunbird is a species of bird in the family Nectariniidae. It is found in a wide range of semi-open wooded habitats in the northern and eastern part of the Philippines. It is often considered a subspecies of the brown-throated sunbird, but the two differ consistently in measurements and plumage, and there is no evidence of intergradation between them.

children.name: Anthreptes longuemarei
children.description: The western violet-backed sunbird or Longuemare's sunbird is a species of bird in the family Nectariniidae. It is the most widely ranging species in the violet-backed sunbird superspecies, ranging throughout a large part of tropical mainland sub-Saharan Africa not inhabited by other members of the superspecies. It is mainly found in regions with mesic woodland.

children.name: Anthreptes malacensis
children.description: The brown-throated sunbird, also known as the plain-throated sunbird, is a species of bird in the family Nectariniidae. It is found in a wide range of semi-open habitats in south-east Asia, ranging from Myanmar to the Lesser Sundas and west Philippines. The grey-throated sunbird found in the remaining part of the Philippines is often considered a subspecies of the brown-throated sunbird, but the two differ consistently in measurements and plumage, and there is no evidence of intergradation between them.

children.name: Anthreptes neglectus

children.name: Anthreptes orientalis

children.name: Histurgops crassirostris
children.description: A large weaver with a thick bill, streaked brown upperparts, white underparts, and a bright rufous tail. It is endemic to the savannas of central Tanzania.

children.name: Foudia
children.description: A genus of weavers endemic to the Indian Ocean islands of Madagascar, the Comoros, and the Seychelles. They are sometimes called fodies and are known for their bright red breeding plumage.

children.name: Foudia madagascariensis
children.description: The red fody (Foudia madagascariensis), also known as the Madagascar fody in Madagascar, red cardinal fody in Mauritius, or common fody, is a small bird native to Madagascar and introduced to various other islands in the Indian Ocean.

children.name: Foudia eminentissima
children.description: The Comoros fody (Foudia eminentissima), also known as the red-headed fody, is a species of passerine bird in the family Ploceidae.

children.name: Foudia albicans
children.description: A fody with a red head and breast, white belly, and brown upperparts. It is endemic to the mountains of northern Madagascar.

children.name: Foudia flavicans
children.description: The Rodrigues fody (Foudia flavicans) is a rare species of bird in the weaver family.

children.name: Foudia rubra
children.description: The Mauritius fody (Foudia rubra) is a rare species of bird in the weaver family.

children.name: Foudia sechellarum
children.description: The Seychelles fody (Foudia sechellarum) is a small yellowish songbird that are native to the Seychelles islands of Cousin Island, Cousine Island, Frégate Island, and have been introduced to Aride Island, D'Arros Island and as of 2004 Denis Island.

children.name: Textor
children.description: A genus of forest-dwelling weavers with black and yellow plumage, found in Central and West Africa.

children.name: Textor capitalis
children.description: A forest weaver with a black head, yellow body, and olive back. It is found in lowland forests of central Africa.

children.name: Textor albiventris
children.description: A forest weaver with a black head, white belly, yellow breast, and olive back. It is found in lowland forests of West Africa.

children.name: Sitagra
children.description: A genus of bright yellow weavers with black or olive heads, found in wetlands and savannas of Africa.

children.name: Sitagra flavoviridis
children.description: A weaver with yellow-green upperparts, bright yellow underparts, and a black bill. It is found in marshes and wetlands of central Africa.

children.name: Sitagra luteola
children.description: A small weaver with yellow underparts, olive upperparts, and a pale bill. It is found in wetlands and grasslands of western Africa.

children.name: Melanoplectus
children.description: A genus of predominantly black weavers with red or yellow markings, found in forests of Central Africa.

children.name: Melanoplectus nigerrimus
children.description: A glossy black weaver with a pale eye, found in lowland forests of central and western Africa.

children.name: Melanoplectus albinuchus
children.description: A black weaver with a white nape patch, found in lowland forests of central Africa.

children.name: Oriolops
children.description: A genus of weavers with bright yellow and black plumage resembling orioles, found in forests of Africa.

children.name: Oriolops aurantius
children.description: A brilliant orange-and-black weaver found in mangroves and coastal forests of West Africa.

children.name: Oriolops sulphureus
children.description: A weaver with sulphur-yellow underparts, black head, and olive back. It is found in lowland forests of central Africa.

children.name: Hyphantornis
children.description: A genus of masked weavers with black face masks and bright yellow bodies, found across Africa.

children.name: Hyphantornis velatus
children.description: A masked weaver with black face, yellow body, and olive back. It is common across southern Africa.

children.name: Hyphantornis nigriceps
children.description: A masked weaver with a black head, yellow body, and olive back. It is found in savannas of East Africa.

children.name: Hyphantornis taenioptera
children.description: A masked weaver with a black face mask, yellow body, and brown back. It is found in the Sahel region of Africa.

children.name: Sycobrotus
children.description: A genus of small weavers with slender bills, found in forests and wetlands of Africa.

children.name: Sycobrotus pelzelni
children.description: A small weaver with a slender bill, yellow underparts, olive upperparts, and a black face mask. It is found in marshes of western and central Africa.

children.name: Sycobrotus xanthopterus
children.description: A weaver with a brown throat, yellow body, and olive back. It is found in wetlands of southern Africa.

children.name: Nelicurvius
children.description: A genus of weavers found on the Mascarene Islands, with red and black plumage in males and brown in females.

children.name: Nelicurvius flavicans
children.description: A small fody with yellow underparts, olive upperparts, and a red bill. It is endemic to Rodrigues Island.

children.name: Nelicurvius ruber
children.description: A small fody with red head and breast in males, brown upperparts, and a red bill. It is endemic to Madagascar.

children.name: Ploceus
children.description: Additional species of typical weavers from Africa and Asia, known for their bright breeding plumages and woven nests.

children.name: Ploceus flavovirens
children.description: A weaver with yellow-green upperparts, bright yellow underparts, and a black bill. It is found in lowland forests of central Africa.

children.name: Ploceus melanoxanthus
children.description: A weaver with a black head and breast, yellow body, and olive back. It is found in lowland forests of central Africa.

children.name: Ploceus nigriventris
children.description: A weaver with a black belly, yellow breast and throat, and olive back. It is found in lowland forests of central Africa.

children.name: Ploceus rufaxillaris
children.description: A weaver with rufous wing patches, yellow body, and olive back. It is found in savannas of central Africa.

children.name: Ploceus fuscus
children.description: A dark weaver with brownish-black plumage and a pale eye. It is found in lowland forests of central Africa.

children.name: Ploceus melanospiza
children.description: A weaver with a black bill, yellow body, and olive back. It is found in marshes of East Africa.

children.name: Ploceus cinnabarinus
children.description: A weaver with a bright cinnabar-red breast and belly, black head, and olive back. It is found in marshes of central Africa.

children.name: Ploceus aurantiacus
children.description: A weaver with an orange back and rump, black head, and yellow underparts. It is found in lowland forests of central Africa.

children.name: Ploceus chrysopterus
children.description: A weaver with golden-yellow wing patches, black head, and yellow body. It is found in wetlands of central Africa.

children.name: Ploceus erythrops
children.description: A weaver with a red face and throat, yellow body, and olive back. It is found in lowland forests of West Africa.

children.name: Ploceus sulfuraceus
children.description: A weaver with sulphur-yellow underparts, olive upperparts, and a black bill. It is found in wetlands of central Africa.

children.name: Ploceus luteolus
children.description: The little weaver (Ploceus luteolus) is a species of bird in the family Ploceidae.

children.name: Ploceus micropteryx
children.description: A weaver with a black head, yellow body, and relatively small wings. It is found in lowland forests of central Africa.

children.name: Ploceus albiventris
children.description: A weaver with a black head, white belly, yellow breast, and olive back. It is found in lowland forests of central Africa.

children.name: Ploceus flavicans
children.description: A weaver with a yellow back and rump, black head, and yellow underparts. It is found in savannas of central Africa.

children.name: Ploceus castaneiceps
children.description: The Taveta weaver (Ploceus castaneiceps), also known as the Taveta golden weaver, (or the mango bird) is a species of bird in the weaver family, Ploceidae.

children.name: Passer
children.description: Intimately associated with human settlement for thousands of years. The House Sparrow has declined catastrophically in western European cities since the 1990s, including Stockholm, probably due to loss of nest sites in modernised buildings and reduced invertebrate food for chicks. The Tree Sparrow is slightly more rural, identified by its chestnut crown and black ear spot.

children.name: Passer domesticus
children.description: The house sparrow is a bird of the sparrow family Passeridae, found in most parts of the world. It is a small bird that has a typical length of 16 cm (6.3 in) and a mass of 24–39.5 g (0.85–1.39 oz). Females and young birds are coloured pale brown and grey, and males have brighter black, white, and brown markings.

children.name: Passer montanus
children.description: The tree sparrow is a passerine bird in the sparrow family with a rich chestnut crown and nape and a black patch on each pure white cheek. The sexes have similar plumage, and young birds are duller versions of the adult. This sparrow breeds across much of temperate Eurasia and Southeast Asia and has been introduced elsewhere, including the United States, where it is known as the Eurasian tree sparrow or German sparrow to differentiate it from the native American tree sparrow.

children.name: Passer ammodendri
children.description: The saxaul sparrow (Passer ammodendri) is a passerine bird of the sparrow family (Passeridae), found in parts of Central Asia.

children.name: Passer castanopterus
children.description: The Somali sparrow (Passer castanopterus) is a species of bird in the family Passeridae found in Somalia, Djibouti, Ethiopia and Kenya.

children.name: Passer cordofanicus
children.description: The Kordofan sparrow (Passer cordofanicus), also known as the Kordofan rufous sparrow, is a sparrow found only in southwestern Sudan and adjacent border regions of South Sudan and Chad.

children.name: Passer eminibey
children.description: The chestnut sparrow (Passer eminibey) is a species of passerine bird in the sparrow family Passeridae.

children.name: Passer griseus
children.description: The northern grey-headed sparrow (Passer griseus), also known as the grey-headed sparrow, is a species of bird in the sparrow family Passeridae, which is resident in much of tropical Africa.

children.name: Passer hispaniolensis
children.description: The Spanish sparrow or willow sparrow (Passer hispaniolensis) is a passerine bird of the sparrow family Passeridae.

children.name: Passer iagoensis
children.description: The Iago sparrow (Passer iagoensis), also known as the Cape Verde or rufous-backed sparrow, is a passerine bird of the sparrow family Passeridae.

children.name: Passer insularis
children.description: The Socotra sparrow (Passer insularis) is a passerine bird endemic to the islands of Socotra, Samhah, and Darsah in the Indian Ocean, off the Horn of Africa.

children.name: Passer italiae
children.description: The Italian sparrow (Passer italiae), also known as the cisalpine sparrow, is a passerine bird of the sparrow family Passeridae, found in Italy and other parts of the Mediterranean region.

children.name: Passer melanurus
children.description: The Cape sparrow (Passer melanurus), or mossie, is a bird of the sparrow family Passeridae found in southern Africa.

children.name: Passer motitensis
children.description: The great sparrow (Passer motitensis), also known as the southern rufous sparrow, is found in southern Africa in dry, wooded savannah and towns.

children.name: Passer pyrrhonotus
children.description: The Sind sparrow (Passer pyrrhonotus) is a passerine bird of the sparrow family, Passeridae, found around the Indus valley region in South Asia.

children.name: Passer rufocinctus
children.description: The Kenya sparrow (Passer rufocinctus), also known as the Kenya rufous sparrow, is a sparrow found in Kenya and Tanzania.

children.name: Passer cinnamomeus
children.description: The russet sparrow (Passer cinnamomeus), also called the cinnamon or cinnamon tree sparrow, is a passerine bird of the sparrow family Passeridae.

children.name: Passer simplex
children.description: The desert sparrow (Passer simplex) is a species of bird in the sparrow family Passeridae, found in the Sahara Desert of northern Africa.

children.name: Passer suahelicus
children.description: The Swahili sparrow (Passer suahelicus) is a passerine bird of the sparrow family Passeridae.

children.name: Gymnoris
children.description: The bush sparrows or rock sparrows, a group of four Afrotropical and Asian species. They are medium-sized sparrows with relatively long tails and pale bills. Males typically have a yellow throat patch, especially conspicuous during the breeding season.

children.name: Petronia
children.description: The Rock Sparrow is the sole member of this genus, a sturdy, streaked bird of rocky hillsides and open stony terrain across southern Europe, North Africa, and Asia. It has a pale bill and a distinctive yellow patch on the breast that is often hard to see.

children.name: Petronia petronia
children.description: The rock sparrow or rock petronia (Petronia petronia) is a small passerine bird in the sparrow family Passeridae.

children.name: Carpospiza
children.description: The Pale Rockfinch is the only species in this genus, a pale, finch-like bird of arid rocky hillsides. It has a thin bill compared to other sparrows and a soft, lark-like song. It breeds from Turkey east to Afghanistan and winters in northeastern Africa.

children.name: Carpospiza brachydactyla
children.description: The pale rockfinch or pale rock sparrow (Carpospiza brachydactyla) is a small sparrow found in the Middle East and Central Asia.

children.name: Hypocryptadius
children.description: The Cinnamon Ibon is an enigmatic passerine endemic to the mountains of Mindanao in the Philippines. Long considered a white-eye, molecular studies have firmly placed it within Passeridae as the most basal sparrow lineage. It forages in forest canopies for insects and fruit.

children.name: Hypocryptadius cinnamomeus
children.description: The cinnamon ibon (Hypocryptadius cinnamomeus) is a species of bird endemic to the mountains of Mindanao in the Philippines.

children.name: Montifringilla
children.description: The snowfinches — sturdy, pale-bodied birds of high-altitude plateaus and mountain slopes. They are well-adapted to cold environments with extensive white in the wings and tail that is flashed in flight. They occur across the high mountains of southern Europe, Central Asia, and the Tibetan Plateau.

children.name: Montifringilla henrici
children.description: The Tibetan snowfinch or Henri's snowfinch (Montifringilla henrici) is a species of bird in the sparrow family.

children.name: Onychostruthus
children.description: The White-rumped Snowfinch is the sole species in this genus, distinguished from Montifringilla by its white rump and unique tail feather structure. It is a high-altitude specialist of the Tibetan Plateau, well-camouflaged against the rocky scree it inhabits.

children.name: Pyrgilauda
children.description: The ground snowfinches — four small, pale snowfinch species that inhabit the high-altitude steppes and rocky slopes of Central Asia and the Tibetan Plateau. They are more terrestrial than Montifringilla and have less white in the wings. Named after the Greek pyrgos (tower) and lauda (lark), reflecting their ground-dwelling habits.

children.name: Pyrgilauda theresae
children.description: The Afghan snowfinch (Pyrgilauda theresae) or the Afghan ground-sparrow, bar-tailed snowfinch, Meinertzhagen's snowfinch, or Theresa's snowfinch, is a passerine bird of the sparrow family Passeridae, endemic to the northern parts of the Hindu Kush mountains in Afghanistan.

children.name: Emberiza
children.description: Seed-eating birds of open habitats. The Yellowhammer's lazy summer song is the defining sound of Swedish farmland hedgerows; it is now declining rapidly across Europe due to agricultural intensification. The Ortolan Bunting has collapsed in Sweden and is the subject of urgent conservation measures.

children.name: Emberiza citrinella
children.description: The yellowhammer is a passerine bird in the bunting family that is native to Eurasia and has been introduced to New Zealand and Australia. Most European birds remain in the breeding range year-round, but the eastern subspecies is partially migratory, with much of the population wintering further south. The male yellowhammer has a bright yellow head, streaked brown back, chestnut rump, and yellow under parts.

children.name: Emberiza schoeniclus
children.description: The common reed bunting, or simply reed bunting, is a passerine bird in the bunting family Emberizidae. This species breeds throughout Europe and much of the Palearctic region. While most individuals migrate south in winter, those in the milder south and west of the range are resident.

children.name: Emberiza hortulana
children.description: The ortolan, also called ortolan bunting, is a Eurasian bird in the bunting family Emberizidae, a passerine family now separated by most modern scholars from the finches, Fringillidae. The genus name Emberiza is from Alemannic German Embritz, a bunting. The specific name hortulana is from the Italian name for this bird, ortolana.

children.name: Emberiza pusilla
children.description: The little bunting is a passerine bird belonging to the bunting family (Emberizidae).

children.name: Emberiza calandra
children.description: The corn bunting is a passerine bird in the bunting family Emberizidae, a group now separated by most modern authors from the finches, Fringillidae. This is a large bunting with heavily streaked buff-brown plumage. The sexes are similar but the male is slightly larger than the female.

children.name: Emberiza cirlus
children.description: thumb| Emberiza cirlus - [[MHNT]] thumb| [[Cuculus canorus|Cuculus canorus canorus in a spawn of Emberiza cirlus - MHNT]].

children.name: Emberiza cia
children.description: The rock bunting (Emberiza cia) is a passerine bird in the bunting family Emberizidae, a group now separated by most modern authors from the finches, Fringillidae.

children.name: Emberiza rustica
children.description: The rustic bunting is a passerine bird in the bunting family Emberizidae, a group now separated by most modern authors from the finches, Fringillidae. The genus name Emberiza is from Old German Embritz, a bunting. The specific rustica is Latin for "rustic, simple".

children.name: Emberiza aureola
children.description: The yellow-breasted bunting is a passerine bird in the bunting family Emberizidae that is found across the Boreal and East Palearctic. The genus name Emberiza is from Old German Embritz, a bunting. The specific aureola is Latin for "golden".

children.name: Emberiza leucocephalos
children.description: The pine bunting (Emberiza leucocephalos) is a passerine bird in the bunting family Emberizidae, a group most modern authors now separate from the finches, Fringillidae.

children.name: Emberiza cioides
children.description: The meadow bunting or Siberian meadow bunting (Emberiza cioides) is a passerine bird of eastern Asia which belongs to the genus Emberiza in the bunting family Emberizidae.

children.name: Emberiza striolata
children.description: The striolated bunting (Emberiza striolata) is a passerine bird in the bunting family Emberizidae, a group now separated by most modern authors from the finches, Fringillidae.

children.name: Emberiza capensis
children.description: The Cape bunting (Emberiza capensis) is a passerine bird in the bunting family Emberizidae.

children.name: Emberiza sulphurata
children.description: :The name "yellow bunting" can also refer to the yellowhammer (Emberiza citrinella).

children.name: Emberiza variabilis
children.description: The grey bunting (Emberiza variabilis) is a species of bird in the family Emberizidae.

children.name: Emberiza koslowi
children.description: The Tibetan bunting (Emberiza koslowi) is a species of bird in the family Emberizidae.

children.name: Emberiza rutila
children.description: The chestnut bunting (Emberiza rutila) is a passerine bird in the bunting family Emberizidae found in the East Palearctic.

children.name: Emberiza siemsseni
children.description: The slaty bunting (Emberiza siemsseni) is a species of bird in the family Emberizidae.

children.name: Emberiza sahari
children.description: The house bunting (Emberiza sahari) is a passerine bird in the bunting family Emberizidae.

children.name: Emberiza poliopleura
children.description: The Somali bunting or Somali golden-breasted bunting (Emberiza poliopleura) is a species of bird in the family Emberizidae.

children.name: Emberiza socotrana
children.description: The Socotra bunting (Emberiza socotrana) is a species of bird in the family Emberizidae.

children.name: Emberiza lathami
children.description: The crested bunting (Emberiza lathami) is a species of bird in the family Emberizidae.

children.name: Plectrophenax
children.description: Hardy buntings of Arctic coasts and tundra, the males strikingly white in summer.

children.name: Plectrophenax nivalis
children.description: The snow bunting is a passerine bird in the family Calcariidae. It is an Arctic specialist, with a circumpolar Arctic breeding range throughout the northern hemisphere. There are small isolated populations on a few high mountain tops south of the Arctic region, including the Cairngorms in central Scotland and the Saint Elias Mountains on the southern Alaska-Yukon border, as well as the Cape Breton Highlands.

children.name: Calcarius
children.description: Ground-dwelling buntings of open tundra, the males with chestnut and black head patterns.

children.name: Calcarius lapponicus
children.description: The Lapland longspur, also known as the Lapland bunting, is a passerine bird in the longspur family Calcariidae. It is a circumpolar arctic breeder and the only member of the genus Calcarius present in Eurasia.

children.name: Rhynchophanes
children.description: A monotypic genus containing McCown's longspur of the North American shortgrass prairie. Formerly placed in Calcarius, it is now recognised as a distinct lineage on genetic grounds. Unlike other longspurs, it nests in loose colonies and performs spectacular aerial display flights.

children.name: Grammatoptila
children.description: A monotypic genus of laughingthrush with boldly striped plumage, found in the Himalayas.

children.name: Grammatoptila striata
children.description: The striated laughingthrush (Grammatoptila striata) is a passerine bird in the family Leiothrichidae.

children.name: Pterorhinus
children.description: A genus of medium to large laughingthrushes with varied plumage, found across East and Southeast Asia.

children.name: Pterorhinus monileger
children.description: A laughingthrush with a narrow black necklace, grey upperparts, and white underparts. It ranges from the Himalayas through Southeast Asia to southern China.

children.name: Pterorhinus lanceolatus
children.description: The Chinese babax (Pterorhinus lanceolatus) is a species of bird in the family Leiothrichidae.

children.name: Pterorhinus waddelli
children.description: The giant babax (Pterorhinus waddelli) is a species of bird in the laughingthrush family Leiothrichidae, found in northeast India and southern Tibet.

children.name: Pterorhinus koslowi
children.description: The Tibetan babax (Pterorhinus koslowi) is a species of bird in the family Leiothrichidae.

children.name: Pterorhinus nigrimentum
children.description: A laughingthrush with a black chin, white face, chestnut crown, and olive-brown body. It inhabits montane forests of southern China and northern Vietnam.

children.name: Pterorhinus poecilorhynchus
children.description: The rusty laughingthrush (Pterorhinus poecilorhynchus) is a species of bird in the family Leiothrichidae.

children.name: Garrulax
children.description: A genus of striking laughingthrushes with bold head patterns, found in Asia.

children.name: Garrulax bicolor
children.description: The Sumatran laughingthrush (Garrulax bicolor), also known as the black-and-white laughingthrush, is a member of the family Leiothrichidae.

children.name: Garrulax ferrugineus
children.description: A laughingthrush with a rufous forehead and crown, grey face, and olive-brown body. It inhabits montane forests of the eastern Himalayas.

children.name: Garrulax leucogaster
children.description: A laughingthrush with a white belly, chestnut crown, black mask, and grey upperparts. It is found in the mountains of southern India.

children.name: Garrulax maurus
children.description: A laughingthrush with a chestnut back and wings, white face, black mask, and grey underparts. It is endemic to the mountains of Sumatra.

children.name: Ianthocincla
children.description: A genus of colourful laughingthrushes with distinctive facial patterns and spotted or ocellated plumage. They are found in montane forests of the Himalayas and China.

children.name: Ianthocincla ocellata
children.description: The spotted laughingthrush (Ianthocincla ocellata) is a bird species in the family Leiothrichidae.

children.name: Leiothrix
children.description: A genus of brightly colored, small to medium-sized birds with melodious songs, found in Asia.

children.name: Actinodura
children.description: A genus of small to medium-sized birds including minlas and barwings, found in montane forests of Asia.

children.name: Actinodura ramsayi
children.description: The spectacled barwing (Actinodura ramsayi) is a species of bird in the family Leiothrichidae.

children.name: Actinodura souliei
children.description: The streaked barwing (Actinodura souliei) is a species of bird in the family Leiothrichidae.

children.name: Actinodura morrisoniana
children.description: The Taiwan barwing or Formosan barwing (Actinodura morrisoniana) is a species of bird in the family Leiothrichidae.

children.name: Minla
children.description: A monotypic genus containing the Red-tailed Minla, a colourful bird of montane forests in East Asia.

children.name: Trochalopteron
children.description: A genus of colorful laughingthrushes with scaled or patterned plumage, found in montane forests of Asia.

children.name: Trochalopteron subunicolor
children.description: The scaly laughingthrush (Trochalopteron subunicolor) is a bird species in the family Leiothrichidae.

children.name: Trochalopteron ocellatum
children.description: The Spotted Laughingthrush has dark plumage with prominent white spots on the breast and head, and rufous-tinged wings. It inhabits rhododendron and oak forests in the Himalayas.

children.name: Trochalopteron chrysopterum
children.description: The Assam laughingthrush (Trochalopteron chrysopterum) is a species of bird in the family Leiothrichidae.

children.name: Trochalopteron imbricatum
children.description: The Bhutan laughingthrush (Trochalopteron imbricatum) is a species of bird in the family Leiothrichidae.

children.name: Trochalopteron lineatum
children.description: The streaked laughingthrush (Trochalopteron lineatum) is a species of bird in the family Leiothrichidae.

children.name: Trochalopteron ludlowi
children.description: A laughingthrush with a grey crown, black mask, olive-brown body, and rufous wings. It is found in the mountains of northeastern India and adjacent Tibet.

children.name: Trochalopteron meridionale
children.description: The Ashambu laughingthrush or Travancore laughingthrush (Montecincla meridionalis) is a species of bird in the family Leiothrichidae.

children.name: Trochalopteron virgatum
children.description: The striped laughingthrush (Trochalopteron virgatum) is a species of bird in the family Leiothrichidae.

children.name: Heterophasia
children.description: A genus of slender, long-tailed birds with melodious songs, known as sibias, found in montane forests of Asia.

children.name: Heterophasia capistrata
children.description: The rufous sibia (Heterophasia capistrata) is a species of bird in the family Leiothrichidae.

children.name: Heterophasia gracilis
children.description: The grey sibia (Heterophasia gracilis) is a species of bird in the family Leiothrichidae.

children.name: Heterophasia pulchella
children.description: The beautiful sibia (Heterophasia pulchella) is a species of bird in the family Leiothrichidae.

children.name: Laniellus
children.description: A small genus of strikingly patterned birds with spotted and streaked plumage, found in montane forests of Southeast Asia. They are related to the sibias and have long, graduated tails.

children.name: Laniellus albonotatus
children.description: The spotted crocias (Laniellus albonotatus) is a passerine bird in the family Leiothrichidae.

children.name: Cutia
children.description: A genus of strikingly patterned birds with barred underparts, found in montane forests of Asia.

children.name: Cutia nipalensis
children.description: The Himalayan cutia (Cutia nipalensis) is a bird species in the family Leiothrichidae.

children.name: Cutia legalleni
children.description: The Vietnamese cutia (Cutia legalleni) is a bird species in the family Leiothrichidae.

children.name: Monteincila

children.name: Artamella
children.description: A monotypic genus of vanga endemic to Madagascar, containing the White-headed Vanga. It has a striking white head contrasting with black wings and tail, and a relatively slender, straight bill adapted for gleaning insects from foliage. It is a social species often seen in small groups.

children.name: Calicalicus
children.description: A genus of small, sexually dimorphic vangas endemic to Madagascar, with males sporting bright red or chestnut patches on the wings and tail. They are among the smallest members of the vanga family and are active, acrobatic foragers in the forest canopy. Their short, stout bills are adapted for gleaning insects from foliage rather than the specialised foraging of other vangas.

children.name: Calicalicus rufocarpalis
children.description: The red-shouldered vanga is a member of the vanga family endemic to south-west Madagascar.

children.name: Cyanolanius
children.description: A monotypic genus of strikingly coloured vanga with brilliant azure-blue upperparts that are unique among Malagasy passerines. It has a relatively slender, straight bill and is more of a canopy insectivore than other vangas. Its distribution extends beyond Madagascar to the Comoros Islands, unusual for the family, which is otherwise entirely restricted to Madagascar.

children.name: Cyanolanius comorensis
children.description: The Comoros blue vanga or Comoro blue vanga is a bird species in the family Vangidae. It is found in the Comoros, where its natural habitats are subtropical or tropical dry forest and subtropical or tropical moist lowland forest.

children.name: Euryceros
children.description: A monotypic genus containing the extraordinary Helmet Vanga, one of the most distinctive birds in Madagascar. It has a massive, deep, laterally compressed bill that is a vivid blue-grey and forms a prominent casque on the forehead. This remarkable adaptation is used to crush large insects and other prey. It is a large, robust vanga of eastern rainforests.

children.name: Euryceros prevostii
children.description: The helmet vanga (Euryceros prevostii) is a distinctive-looking bird of the vanga family, Vangidae, and is classified in its own genus, Euryceros.

children.name: Falculea
children.description: A monotypic vanga genus containing the Sickle-billed Vanga, which possesses the most extreme bill morphology in the family: a long, slender, strongly decurved bill resembling a sickle. This highly specialised tool is used to probe deep into tree crevices and bark furrows for large insects. Endemic to Madagascar, it is the largest species in the vanga family.

children.name: Hypositta
children.description: A monotypic genus of small vanga containing the Nuthatch Vanga, which convergently resembles a nuthatch in both morphology and behaviour. It has a short, straight bill and strong feet, and is unique among vangas for its tree-creeping foraging style, spiralling up trunks and branches in search of insects. Endemic to Madagascar.

children.name: Hypositta corallirostris
children.description: The nuthatch vanga (Hypositta corallirostris), also known as the coral-billed nuthatch-vanga and formerly as the coral-billed nuthatch, is a species of bird in the family Vangidae.

children.name: Leptopterus
children.description: A monotypic genus of vanga containing the Chabert Vanga, a small, pale-eyed species endemic to Madagascar. It has a relatively slender, straight bill and is an active canopy insectivore, often joining mixed-species flocks. Its pale blue-grey plumage makes it one of the more subtly coloured vangas.

children.name: Leptopterus chabert
children.description: thumb|Chabert vanga near Toliara, SW Madagascar The chabert vanga (Leptopterus chabert), also erroneously called "Chabert's vanga", is a species of bird in the family Vangidae.

children.name: Mystacornis
children.description: A monotypic genus of terrestrial vanga endemic to Madagascar, containing Crossley's Vanga. It has a long, slender, slightly decurved bill and strong legs, adapted for a ground-foraging lifestyle in the leaf litter of the forest floor. It is one of the most secretive and poorly known members of the vanga family.

children.name: Newtonia

They were traditionally placed in the Old World warbler family Sylviidae before molecular studies revealed their true affinities within the vanga family. They are insectivorous birds of forest and scrub habitats.

They are restricted to Australia, inhabiting heathlands, swamps, and sedgelands. Their weak flight and skulking behaviour make them notoriously difficult to observe.

children.name: Amytornis

They have strong legs and relatively long tails, and are notoriously difficult to observe due to their skulking behaviour. Their cryptic plumage and weak flight make them among Australia's most challenging birds to study.

children.name: Regulus
children.description: Kinglets and firecrests — Europe's and North America's smallest birds, weighing as little as 5 grams yet capable of surviving Scandinavian winters in spruce forest by constant foraging through the night. The goldcrest (kungsfågel — 'king bird') takes its royal name from the brilliant gold and orange crown stripe that is erected into a crest during display and aggressive encounters: the English 'goldcrest' and Latin Regulus ('little king') both reflect this crown. The goldcrest breeds in almost every Swedish spruce forest and migrates in vast numbers each autumn, moving in loose mixed flocks with tits through the coastal zone; in some years hundreds of thousands cross the Swedish coast on a single October day. The firecrest, with its additional white supercilium and blazing orange crown, is slowly expanding northward into southern Sweden as temperatures warm.

children.name: Menura

The male's extraordinary tail, shaped like a Greek lyre when fanned, is the most elaborate of any bird. They can imitate any sound — from other birds' songs to chainsaws, camera shutters, and car alarms — with astonishing fidelity. Despite their superb mimicry, lyrebirds are rarely seen, spending most of their time scratching through forest leaf litter for invertebrates.
